notes.meaning: Believers are told to keep on loving one another as brothers and sisters in God's family. This special affection already existed among them, but they needed to guard it carefully. Disagreements and hard times could easily make their love grow cold if they did not actively practice it.

Christians should always be ready to welcome travelers and strangers into their homes. In Bible times, inns were often dangerous and immoral, so traveling believers relied on the kindness of others. In the past, faithful men like Abraham and Lot showed hospitality to strangers and discovered they had welcomed angels without knowing it.

The church must care for fellow believers who have been locked up for their faith, treating them as if they were sharing the same chains. Christians must also show deep sympathy to anyone who is mistreated. Since believers still live in human bodies, they should remember that they could easily face the very same suffering.

Marriage is an honorable state created by God and should be respected by everyone. Husbands and wives are called to stay completely faithful to one another. Those who commit sexual sin outside of marriage or break their marriage vows will face God's sure judgment.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching honors marriage as a sacred bond for the laity, but also teaches that consecrated celibacy for religious life and the priesthood is a higher calling.

notes.meaning: Believers must not let greed or the love of money rule their lives. Instead, they should be satisfied and peaceful with whatever they currently have. Real contentment does not come from wealth, but from God's personal promise that He will never abandon or forsake His people.

Because God is always near to help, Christians can speak with bold confidence and reject fear. Human beings may threaten or harm our physical bodies, but they have no power over our eternal safety. Trusting in the Lord makes the soul fearless in the face of danger.

Christians should fondly remember their past spiritual leaders who first brought them the word of God. Believers are told to look closely at how those leaders lived and how they finished their earthly journey faithfully. Seeing their good example should encourage the church to copy their steadfast faith.

Jesus Christ never changes in His nature, His promises, or His saving power. He was the Savior yesterday for past generations, He is the same today for us, and He will remain the same forever into eternity. Because He never shifts, believers can place complete and lasting trust in His unchanging truth.

The author warns believers not to drift away after novel and strange teachings that stray from Christ. True spiritual strength comes from God's free grace—His undeserved favor—and not from religious food rules or ceremonial diets. Those ancient dietary rituals never gave real spiritual profit or cleansed the conscience of those who observed them.

Christians possess a spiritual altar and sacrifice that those still serving the old Jewish tent worship have no right to share. Our altar is Christ and His finished work on the cross. Those who insist on trusting in the old temple rites cut themselves off from the blessings of this new and better sacrifice.

differ.view: Some Anglicans see this as feeding spiritually on Christ in the Eucharist, while still looking to the cross as the true sacrifice.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: The altar is understood as the Eucharistic altar of the New Covenant where the sacrifice of the Mass or Divine Liturgy is celebrated.

notes.meaning: Under the law of Moses, the high priest took the blood of specific animals into the inner sanctuary to pay for sin. Yet the priests were never permitted to eat the meat of those offerings. Instead, the bodies of those animals had to be carried completely outside the camp and burned to ashes.

Jesus fulfilled the ancient pattern of that special sin offering by being crucified outside the city gate of Jerusalem. His purpose was to sanctify His people—which means to cleanse them from sin and set them apart for God. He accomplished this ultimate cleansing not with animal blood, but with His very own blood.

Believers are urged to leave behind the old religious camp and go out to Jesus where He was crucified. Following Him means being willing to be rejected by the world just as He was. We must gladly accept the shame and disgrace that come from being identified with our Savior.

Christians do not have a lasting or permanent home in this present earthly world. Earthly cities, even places like Jerusalem, eventually fade away or are destroyed. Instead, believers live as temporary travelers who are looking ahead to the eternal city that God is preparing for them.

Because Jesus paid for our sins once and for all, we no longer bring animal sacrifices to God. Instead, through Jesus our High Priest, we continually offer up the sacrifice of praise. This is the fruit of our lips, openly giving thanks to God and speaking honor to His name.

True worship must not stop at spoken praise; it must also show itself in practical life. Believers must never forget to do good deeds and share their resources with those in need. God is deeply pleased when His people offer these loving acts of kindness as sacrifices to Him.

Church members are instructed to follow and willingly yield to their spiritual leaders who guide them according to God's word. These leaders carry a serious responsibility to watch over souls, and they will one day have to give an account to God for their work. Believers should cooperate so that pastors can do this duty with gladness rather than with heavy groaning, which would only hurt the congregation.

The writer asks the believers to pray faithfully for him and his ministry partners. He reassures them that he has a clean conscience and truly desires to live an honorable, godly life in every situation. Even faithful teachers need the earnest prayers of God's people to sustain them.

The author pleads even more strongly for their prayers so that he can visit them again without delay. Something beyond his control was keeping him away, and he trusted that their prayers could help open the door for his quick return. Believers should ask God directly for the blessings and reunions they hope to receive.

God is the author and source of true peace, having made reconciliation possible between Himself and sinners. He brought back Jesus from the dead as the great Shepherd who cares for the flock of His church. This victory was secured through Christ's shed blood, which sealed the eternal covenant of salvation.

The writer prays that God will fully equip and prepare the believers with every good thing needed to obey His will. Any good thought or deed in us is actually God's own work through Jesus Christ. All eternal honor and glory belong to Christ for carrying out this saving work in our hearts.

The author asks his readers to receive his letter of encouragement and warning with patience and an open heart. Even though this letter discusses deep and serious truths, he considers it relatively brief compared to the greatness of the subject. Christians should never grow tired of hearing sound instruction and godly warnings.

The writer shares good news that their fellow worker Timothy has just been released from confinement. If Timothy arrives where the author is staying soon enough, both of them will make the trip together to see the church. The freedom of faithful ministers was a cause for shared joy among all the believers.

The letter asks that warm greetings be passed along to all the church's spiritual leaders and to every believer in the congregation. Christians from Italy who were staying with the author also send their love. True faith builds deep bonds of courtesy and affection among believers wherever they live.

The letter concludes with a short and loving blessing asking for God's grace to be with all of them. Grace is God's unearned favor and spiritual power working in the heart. It is the beginning, strength, and perfection of the entire Christian life.
